prompts.text: As you begin, notice what you are carrying from today. Hope, worry, gratitude, fatigue. Reflect on this.
Pause and name a gift you received today, small or large: insight, kindness, encouragement.
Was there a moment when you felt deeply connected, to a person, a task, a role?
What moments today stirred discomfort, tension, or inner questioning, challenging what you expected or wanted?
Did you notice any assumptions or beliefs being tested today? What was challenged? How did you react?
Where did you sense hope, healing, compassion or care during the experience?
What, if anything, made you feel uneasy or distant from your calling, or sense of purpose today?
As you reflect, notice any stirring toward your future? Is there a moment of confidence or uncertainty?
Was there a moment today that stood out to you? What did it stir in your heart?
Was there a moment when you hesitated to engage or act? What held you back?
Were you aware of another's vulnerability or need? If so, how did that make you feel? To care? To act?
What part of today made you feel conected to or more certain about your path, purpose, or calling?
What did today show you about compassion and humility, service, or justice? Does this inform who you want to become?
Did you question your vocational interest or motivation today? What is it?
What intention or commitment do you want to carry forward on your path or for your next experience?
What would you most want to say to God about what you experienced today? Reflect honestly.
What aspect of today's experience, positive or difficult, do you want to remember, and why?
What first struck you today? Was there anything that caught your attention?
What was your first thought in reflecting on today? What do you think sparked that feeling?
Was there a person or someone you encountered that stood out? What stood out and why?
What expectations or assumptions did you bring into today's experience? What was the reality? What do you recall?
When did you feel fully present today? What brought you into that moment?
Recall a moment or an interaction you had today and consider what insights it brought you.
What was the most memorable informal or unexpected intereaction you had today, and why did it stick with you?
As you watched the people around you today, was there a moment that moved you, something that touched you?
What moment today brought tension or discomfort? What is it asking you to look at honestly?
Was there a belief or expectation that was quietly challenged today? Notice what that stirring feels like.
In what situation did you notice your own fears or hesitations, and what did you learn about yourself from that?
What surprised you today? Not just an unexpected happening, but a feeling, an awareness?
How did today's experience connect to your sense of calling or purpose in your profession?
Where today did you witness someone carrying a heavy weight, physical, emotional, or spiritual?
Was there a moment today that affirmed something about your path, not certainty, but a small yes?
Of everything you noticed today, what stays with you? Consider why.
If you could carry just one thing from today into tomorrow what would it be?
What intentions do you want to set for your future learning after this experience?
As you look toward tomorrow, what do you need? Courage, patience, clarity, rest?
Consider re-reading your earlier notes, look for what stands out.
Ask for the grace to let go of wants and fears; then notice what God reveals as true in this experience.
Where did you sense God, grace, or the sacred at work in your experience today?
What troubled your spirit today, or where did you feel inner resistance?
Was there a moment today when you felt distant from grace, hope, or connection with others?
What is the Spirit or your inner wisdom inviting you to see in the experiences you just reviewed?
What prayer, petition, or desire rises from within you as you consider today's challenges and gifts?
What specific grace or strength do you need to ask for as you look toward tomorrow?
Offer a closing prayer of gratitude for this day, its gifts, struggles, and graces.
When you think about the type of professional you want to become, did any moment today exemplify that ideal?
What professional skill, interaction, or attitude stood out to you today as something you wish to emulate?
What is one concrete way you can show up more fully tomorrow in your work, your relationships, or your own growth?
How will the lessons of today inform the way you approach your studies, training, or interactions with others moving forward?
Before you review the day, pause. Name three gifts as simple as a kind word, finishing a task, or the strength to keep going.
Where today did you feel most alive, most yourself, or most drawn toward your purpose? What was happening, and what stirred in you?
Where today did you fall short of who you want to be, in patience, courage, attention, or care?
What stirred in you today? Gratitude, doubt, awe, tension, tenderness? Which feeling is strongest now? What does it reveal?
As you close, notice what you want to place in God's hands? A worry, a hope, a person, a question.
Set aside what you hoped today would be. What was true, as it actually happened?
Before you review your day, let go of what you wanted or feared. What is here when you become still?
Keep your mind open. As you reflect, welcome insights not influenced by want or desire.
Gently set down what you wanted today to go well or feared might not. From this open place, what do you notice?
Before you begin, let go of how you wish today had gone. Simply be here, open to what surfaces.
What did you learn today about the profession you observed? What drew you in or gave you pause?
Was there a moment during shadowing that showed you something about patient care, or the profession? What do you recall?
What drew you closer to patient care today? Was there an interaction you want to return to?
In the clinical setting today, what challenged your understanding of what it means to care for someone?
What offered you a sense of connection through your service today? A person, a task, or a moment?
Who did you serve today, and what did their experience teach you about your own life or calling?
What question or discovery captivated you today? Why does it stay with you?
Where in today's work did you sense the connection between your research and the people it might one day serve?
What responsibility did you feel today as a leader? Was there a decision or moment where you sensed its weight?
Who looked to you for guidance today, and what did that reveal about the kind of leader you are becoming?
What skill, insight, or interaction from your work today surprised you or taught you something new?
Was there a moment at work where you glimpsed the kind of professional or person you are growing into?
Choose one feature of today? A person or a moment? What does it ask of you?
Ask for the grace to let go of comparison, urgency, and fear; receive this discernment time as it is.
As you begin, what desire or fear feels loudest about your vocational path right now?
In prayer, ask for inner freedom. What becomes clearer when you release the need to force an answer?
Name three gifts from this season of discernment: people, experiences, or moments of clarity.
What part of your current path has strengthened your trust in who you are becoming?
Where have you noticed grace accompanying your vocational questions lately?
Which recent challenge has quietly formed you for service, and what are you grateful for in it?
When have you recently felt alive, peaceful, or energized while exploring this path?
When have you felt drained, restless, or diminished while considering this path?
Where do ego, fear, or external pressure seem to cloud your discernment today?
Which assumptions about success or worth are being tested as you discern your next step?
Looking across your recent experiences, what pattern keeps repeating and asking for attention?
What option currently seems to bear more peace, freedom, and love?
In prayer, what truth do you sense God inviting you to trust about your calling right now?
What counsel would you give a close friend in your exact situation, and what does that reveal for you?
What is one concrete next step you can take in the next 7 days to test this path faithfully?
What will you continue, what will you pause, and what will you seek next in your discernment?
Place your uncertainty before God. What grace do you need for the next step?
How will you review the fruit of your next step so discernment stays grounded in reality?
Ask for freedom from fear and ambition; where are you being invited to see medicine truthfully today?
What gift today strengthened your desire to care for the whole person, not just disease?
Where did you feel drawn toward the responsibilities of medicine with peace and clarity?
Where did you feel resistance or unrest about medicine, and what might that unrest be teaching you?
What is one faithful next step in discerning medicine, and what grace do you need to take it?
Ask for a clear heart as you discern dentistry beyond status or outcome.
What moment today made you grateful for the chance to restore comfort, confidence, or dignity?
Where did you sense real desire for the precision and patient trust dentistry requires?
Where did you feel hesitation about the demands of dentistry, and what truth surfaced there?
What next step can help you discern dentistry with honesty and generosity?
Ask for freedom to discern pharmacy in light of service, safety, and truth.
What moment today made you grateful for the role of careful stewardship in medication use?
Where did you feel drawn to pharmacy's blend of science, counseling, and responsibility?
Where did you feel uncertainty about this path, and what does that reveal about your motivations?
What is one concrete next step toward discerning pharmacy with wisdom?
Ask for openness as you discern whether restoring daily function is part of your calling.
What gift today made you grateful for work that helps people regain meaningful daily life?
Where did you feel most aligned with OT's focus on participation, adaptation, and dignity?
Where did you feel tension about this path, and what might be getting clarified through it?
What faithful next step can deepen your discernment of occupational therapy?
Ask for inner freedom as you discern a vocation of healing through movement and persistence.
What moment today made you grateful for the possibility of helping others recover function?
Where did you feel drawn to PT's long-term relational and rehabilitative work?
Where did doubt arise about the demands of PT, and what truth did it uncover?
What next step will help you discern physical therapy with courage and clarity?
Ask for openness to discern a path of collaborative care without attachment to image.
What grace today made you grateful for team-based care and adaptable service?
Where did you feel most drawn to the PA role's flexibility and shared responsibility?
Where did resistance surface, and what does it reveal about your readiness for this path?
What one step can you take now to discern physician assistant practice faithfully?
Ask for freedom from ego and fear as you discern service through law.
What moment today made you grateful for truth-telling, advocacy, or justice?
Where did you feel genuine desire to use legal training for the good of others?
Where did you notice tension between ambition and service, and what did you learn?
What faithful next step will help you discern whether law is your path?
Ask for a clear spirit as you discern care for animals, people, and communities.
What gift today made you grateful for the vocation of veterinary care?
Where did you feel most drawn to veterinary work's compassion, science, and responsibility?
Where did strain appear in this calling, and what truth emerged in that strain?
What concrete next step will move your veterinary discernment forward with honesty?
Ask for openness as you discern a path of restoring sight and attentive care.
What moment today made you grateful for work that improves daily life through vision care?
Where did you feel most alive in the precision and continuity of optometric care?
Where did uncertainty arise, and what is it asking you to examine?
What is one faithful step you can take to test and clarify this calling?
Ask for humility and freedom as you discern your path within advanced training.
What gift today made you grateful for the privilege and burden of deeper responsibility?
Where did you sense alignment between your strengths and the demands of residency?
Where did fatigue, fear, or misalignment appear, and what truth did it expose?
What next faithful action will help you discern your direction within residency training?
Ask for grace to release pressure and listen for what is most true in your life right now.
What gifts from today are you most grateful for as you discern your direction?
Where did you feel most alive, free, and drawn toward love or service today?
Where did you feel divided or restless, and what might that be revealing?
What one faithful step can you take tomorrow in response to what you noticed?
